_about: Demo tour. Sources: verification/catalogue/pages/hindley-milner.md (its sources: list is the backbone), research/mastery-20260927/demos-algorithms.md §3.2; every claim re-checked against the code at HEAD 8479634adc. The comparison with ctype.ml was checked against typing/ctype.ml and typing/btype.ml at the same commit (Tlink, generic_level, update_level, Btype.with_new_pool / add_to_pool, For_copy.redirect_desc with Tsubst).
_note_pools: demos-algorithms.md §3.2 says the per-level pools 'replace OCaml's whole-type traversal'. At HEAD OxCaml's own generalization also uses per-level pools (Btype.pool_stack, with_new_pool, add_to_pool; Ctype.with_local_level_gen), so the tour describes the demo's pools as mirroring those.
title: Hindley–Milner type inference
summary: `Hm_inference.infer` infers types for a small ML with let-polymorphism, using a graph of mutable type nodes with union-find links, levels, per-level pools for generalization and copying for instantiation: a miniature of `typing/ctype.ml`. It is proved sound and principal against a declarative typing relation, so a rejection means the term has no type. The tour goes from the interface and the declarative system, through a client and a rejected client, to the type graph, the relational specification of the algorithm, the runtime code for `let`, the completeness proof and the trusted base.
Only normal return is specified: `infer` is not `total`, may raise, and is not proved to terminate. The [catalogue page](demo:hindley-milner) states the claim, scope and trusted base.

stops.title: The interface: four theorems about one result
stops.text: `result` is abstract; `source` gives the inferred term (erased) and `inferred_type` the answer. `infer` is the only runtime function, and it is not `@@ total`. `sound` returns the typing derivation itself, erased. `principal` states an existential in continuation-passing form, because refinements have no existential quantifier: any `claim` that follows from `inferred_type out = Some ty` and `target = substitute delta ty`, for an arbitrary substitution `delta`, holds. `rejected` is its `None` case: a term that `infer` rejects has no typing at any type.

stops.title: The contract: a declarative typing relation
stops.to: && typed n (Binding (s, g)) b t body
stops.text: `typed n g e t d` holds when the derivation tree `d` shows that `e` has type `t` in context `g`, with `n` type parameters in scope; it is an ordinary total function over an `[@@inductive]` datatype of derivations. `Variable args` instantiates a scheme by `open_scheme`; `Abstraction` and `Recursion` bind monomorphic schemes `Forall (Z, a)`. `Let_binding` is where generalization happens: the right-hand side is typed under `add k n` parameters and `weaken_context k g`, so the new parameters are de Bruijn-shifted in. Type variables of an inferred type appear here as `Free p` constants, through `embed`.

stops.title: A client proof
stops.text: The client uses only the public interfaces. The `scoped_term_def` calls in the first `ghost_` block prove that `λx. x` is closed, the precondition of `infer`. It builds a derivation that `λx. x` has type `bool → bool` (`identity_typing`, above) and passes it to `principal` with `claim = not (inferred_type out === None)`; the continuation `use` is trivial because `principal` already rules out `None`. The refined `ty` then records statically that inference succeeded, so the `failwith` branch is dead. The last lines check at run time that `λx. x x` is rejected; that part is a test.

stops.title: A rejected client
stops.text: `Verified_hm` is the internal module behind `Hm_inference`; its `infer` returns an unboxed record whose `root` is the inferred type's node, or `None` on failure. This client claims that inference always fails, and the checker rejects it with a counterexample because the contract allows `Some`. The same file rejects a forged `V.Spec.evidence` and uses of `principal` and `elaborate` with an unrelated input. [`hm_inference_rejected.ml`](src:testsuite/tests/vox/hm_inference_rejected.ml) checks that the evidence inside `Hm_inference.result` cannot be read: `out.evidence` is an unbound field.

stops.title: The type graph: a miniature of type_expr
stops.from: type level = Generic | Finite of int
stops.to: | Arrow (a, b) -> rho p === Function (rho a, rho b) | Link q -> rho p === rho q)
stops.text: Each type node is a `Pref` cell in a ghost heap `node Pref.heap`. `Link` plays the role of `Tlink`, `Generic` of `generic_level`, and `memo`/`Forward` of the `Tsubst` redirection that `ctype.ml` installs while copying; `visited` is the occurs check's mark bit. Inferred types `ty` have `Variable of node Pref.t`: a type variable is a heap location. `equation h rho p` says that `rho : node Pref.t -> ty` respects node `p`; a function satisfying it at every node is a *model* of the heap, and the completeness proof works with models where textbook proofs use most general unifiers.

stops.title: The algorithm as a relation: let over the heap
stops.from: | RLet_left (rhs, _) -> ran h (depth + 1) Empty env rhs after final_pool
stops.text: `ran h depth pool env e after final_pool` is a big-step specification of algorithm J over the heap, with one constructor of the `execution` datatype per inference case. For `let`, the right-hand side runs one level deeper with an empty pool. `close_heap middle depth child_pool` then generalizes: every node of the child's pool whose level exceeds `depth` becomes `Generic` (`Generalize_spec.closed_heap`), and `transfer_rep` moves the surviving representatives to the parent's pool. The invariant `covered` in [`generalize_spec.ml`](src:testsuite/tests/vox/generalize_spec.ml), that every node above the cut is in the pool, is what lets a pool stand in for a traversal of the whole type, as `Btype.with_new_pool` does in OxCaml.

stops.title: The runtime code for let
stops.text: `work`, most of this 1,241-line file, is the inference itself: continuation-passing code that mutates real `Pref` cells through a unique token and builds the ghost `execution` alongside. Its postcondition is `ran` on that execution. At `let` it raises `Failure` through the `raise_any` external if the level would overflow, saves the current pool in the per-level array (`Rp.save`) and starts the child with an empty pool. After the right-hand side, `Rp.close_and_route` generalizes the child's pool and routes the surviving nodes to their levels' pools. Universally quantified invariants such as `facts` and `trees` are passed as ghost functions over nodes, because the logic has no quantifiers.

stops.title: The core proof: completeness by induction over the execution
stops.text: `with_run_model` is Damas–Milner completeness. Given a run of the algorithm, a model `rho` of the heap before it, and a declarative derivation `d` of the term at `target` in a context `g` that `realize` relates to the environment's templates, it produces a model `tau` of the heap after the run that agrees with `rho` on the old nodes and sends the result to `target`. `closed_completes`, at the end of the file, starts it from the empty heap with the model `fun _ -> Boolean` and concludes that the run did not fail. `closed_factor` adds `Level_mgu_proofs.readback_factor`, which gives `target = substitute rho inferred`: principality.

stops.title: The public result seals its evidence
stops.text: `Hm_inference.result` keeps only the type at run time; the input and the `Verified_hm` evidence (execution, heap, finite readback tree, typing) are ghost fields, and the refinement on `result` ties them together. `infer` wraps `Verified_hm.infer_type`, and `sound` reads the derivation out of the evidence. Further down, `principal` defers to `Verified_hm.principal_evidence`, and `rejected` is `principal` with `claim = false`. The finite readback tree is there because the logic is quantifier-free: that the graph under a node is acyclic and unfolds to a type has to be a concrete ghost tree checked by `finite`.

stops.title: The trusted base
stops.text: Beyond the shared base (the checker, Z3, the compiler, and the contracts of `Pref` and `Borrow_iarray`), the demo trusts these `external` declarations, whose refined types the checker assumes, and `get` at the top of the file. The per-level pools live in a `Borrow_iarray.Owned_array` whose contents the contracts describe with `Vox_iarray.updated`, which calls `set`. `extensional` is assumed: arrays that agree at every index, shown by a ghost function, are equal. The other trusted declaration is `raise_any`, the layout-polymorphic `%raise` in [`hm_routed_infer.ml`](src:testsuite/tests/vox/hm_routed_infer.ml); the `unreachable_ ()` arms of the algorithm add nothing to this list, since the checker proves each unreachable and a run-time trap remains.
